pages.name: Which way
pages.task: The driver turns clockwise. Which way will the 20-tooth gear turn?
pages.why: At the mesh, the driver's right-hand teeth move down. They push the 20-tooth gear's left-hand teeth down too. Teeth moving down on its left side turn it anticlockwise.
pages.alt: The 12-tooth driver turning clockwise, a 20-tooth gear turning anticlockwise.

pages.name: Teeth pass one for one
pages.text: The 12-tooth driver turns clockwise and the 20-tooth gear turns anticlockwise. An arrow at the mesh shows the teeth of both gears moving down together. The two counters at the mesh always show the same count.
pages.alt: The 12-tooth driver turning clockwise, a 20-tooth gear turning anticlockwise. The two counters at a mesh read 24 and 24 teeth passed. An arrow at the mesh shows the teeth of both gears moving down together.

pages.name: Five in a line
pages.task: The first gear turns clockwise. Which way does the fifth turn?
pages.why: Five gears make four meshes, so there are four flips: anticlockwise, clockwise, anticlockwise, clockwise. So the fifth turns the driver's way.
pages.alt: The 12-tooth driver turning clockwise, a 10-tooth gear turning anticlockwise, a 14-tooth gear turning clockwise, a 10-tooth gear turning anticlockwise, a 12-tooth gear turning clockwise.

pages.name: Mixed sizes
pages.task: The 12-tooth driver turns clockwise. Which way does the fourth gear turn?
pages.why: Three meshes make three flips, so the fourth turns anticlockwise. The big 40-tooth gear turns slower, but it still flips the direction once.
pages.alt: The 12-tooth driver turning clockwise, a 40-tooth gear turning anticlockwise, a 16-tooth gear turning clockwise, a 30-tooth gear turning anticlockwise.

pages.name: A bent chain
pages.task: Six gears zigzag across the board. The driver turns clockwise. Which way does the last gear turn?
pages.why: Six gears make five meshes, so there are five flips. Five flips leave the last gear turning anticlockwise, against the driver. Where the gears sit makes no difference.
pages.alt: The 10-tooth driver turning clockwise, a 10-tooth gear turning anticlockwise, a 10-tooth gear turning clockwise, a 10-tooth gear turning anticlockwise, a 10-tooth gear turning clockwise, a 10-tooth gear turning anticlockwise.

pages.name: Odd and even
pages.text: Each mesh flips the direction, so the arrows alternate along a line. An odd number of gears turns the last one the driver's way. An even number turns it the other way.
pages.alt: The 10-tooth driver turning clockwise, a 10-tooth gear turning anticlockwise. The 10-tooth driver turning clockwise, a 10-tooth gear turning anticlockwise, a 10-tooth gear turning clockwise. The 10-tooth driver turning clockwise, a 10-tooth gear turning anticlockwise, a 10-tooth gear turning clockwise, a 10-tooth gear turning anticlockwise. The 10-tooth driver turning clockwise, a 10-tooth gear turning anticlockwise, a 10-tooth gear turning clockwise, a 10-tooth gear turning anticlockwise, a 10-tooth gear turning clockwise.

pages.name: Close the loop
pages.text: The triangle of three is locked, its last mesh drawn in red, and the ring of four turns.
pages.alt: The 12-tooth driver trying to turn clockwise, a 12-tooth gear trying to turn anticlockwise, a 12-tooth gear trying to turn clockwise. This loop is locked, its last mesh drawn in red. The 12-tooth driver turning clockwise, a 12-tooth gear turning anticlockwise, a 12-tooth gear turning clockwise, a 12-tooth gear turning anticlockwise.

pages.name: Which loop turns
pages.task: Three loops lie flat on the board, of five, six and seven gears. Which loop turns?
pages.why: Six is even, so the sixth gear turns opposite to the first, as their mesh needs. Five and seven are odd, so those loops lock, whatever the gears' sizes.
pages.alt: The 8-tooth driver trying to turn clockwise, a 8-tooth gear trying to turn anticlockwise, a 8-tooth gear trying to turn clockwise, a 8-tooth gear trying to turn anticlockwise, a 8-tooth gear trying to turn clockwise. This loop is locked, its last mesh drawn in red. The 8-tooth driver turning clockwise, a 8-tooth gear turning anticlockwise, a 8-tooth gear turning clockwise, a 8-tooth gear turning anticlockwise, a 8-tooth gear turning clockwise, a 8-tooth gear turning anticlockwise. The 8-tooth driver trying to turn clockwise, a 8-tooth gear trying to turn anticlockwise, a 8-tooth gear trying to turn clockwise, a 8-tooth gear trying to turn anticlockwise, a 8-tooth gear trying to turn clockwise, a 8-tooth gear trying to turn anticlockwise, a 8-tooth gear trying to turn clockwise. This loop is locked, its last mesh drawn in red.

pages.name: Count the teeth
pages.text: Three turns of the 12-tooth driver pass 36 teeth and turn the 36-tooth gear once.
pages.alt: The 12-tooth driver turning clockwise, a 36-tooth gear turning anticlockwise. The two counters at a mesh read 36 and 36 teeth passed.

pages.name: How fast
pages.task: A 12-tooth gear turns at 60 rev/min and drives a 36-tooth gear. How fast does the 36-tooth gear turn?
pages.why: 60 × 12 = 720 teeth a minute pass the mesh. Then 720 ÷ 36 = 20 rev/min.
pages.alt: The 12-tooth driver turning clockwise, a 36-tooth gear turning anticlockwise.

pages.name: The idler
pages.text: A 20-tooth idler sits between them and turns at 36 rev/min. The 36-tooth gear still turns at 20 rev/min, now the driver's way.
pages.alt: The 12-tooth driver turning clockwise, a 20-tooth gear turning anticlockwise, a 36-tooth gear turning clockwise. The two counters at a mesh read 18 and 18 teeth passed. The two counters at a mesh read 18 and 18 teeth passed.

pages.name: Through an idler
pages.task: A 15-tooth gear at 1200 rev/min drives a 40-tooth idler. The idler drives a 45-tooth gear. How fast does the 45-tooth gear turn?
pages.why: 1200 × 15 = 18,000 teeth a minute pass both meshes. Then 18,000 ÷ 45 = 400 rev/min. The idler only flips the direction.
pages.alt: The 15-tooth driver turning clockwise, a 40-tooth gear turning anticlockwise, a 45-tooth gear turning clockwise.

pages.name: The drum
pages.task: A motor turns an 18-tooth gear at 1440 rev/min. It drives a 72-tooth gear on a drum. How fast does the drum turn?
pages.alt: The 18-tooth driver turning clockwise, a 72-tooth gear turning anticlockwise.

pages.name: How many teeth
pages.task: A 24-tooth gear turns at 300 rev/min. The gear it drives must turn at 100 rev/min. How many teeth does that gear need?
pages.alt: The 24-tooth driver turning clockwise, a 72-tooth gear turning anticlockwise.

pages.name: Add a fifth
pages.task: You fit a fifth gear into the ring. What happens when you turn the driver?
pages.why: Five is odd. So round the ring, the fifth gear and the first both try to turn the same way. Nothing moves, whatever the sizes.
pages.alt: The 12-tooth driver trying to turn clockwise, a 12-tooth gear trying to turn anticlockwise, a 12-tooth gear trying to turn clockwise, a 12-tooth gear trying to turn anticlockwise, a 12-tooth gear trying to turn anticlockwise. This loop is locked, its last mesh drawn in red.
